subject: Pricing realignment & renewal — proposal for EdgeWave
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Lena Cruz <lena@edgewave.com>
Date: 2028-10-01T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing realignment & renewal — proposal for EdgeWave

Hi Lena,

Hope you're well — congrats again on the new feature launch. Per our conversation last week I pulled together a first-pass approach to align renewal economics with EdgeWave's growth trajectory. High level:

- Objective: keep unit economics predictable for EdgeWave while preserving headroom for the Q4 usage spike.
- Proposal preview: 12-month renewal window, base commit + burst ladder, temporary 6-month price hold on per-token rates, one-time onboarding credit to offset migration of two new ML services.

I attached the Q3 usage export to show the recent consumption pattern (notably the two traffic spikes tied to the search index refresh). Can you confirm who on procurement we should include? I want to align on a clean mutual action plan so we don't lose time in their review loop.

If it's helpful I'd propose a short 30-min call next week to walk the numbers with you and Ray.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: EdgeWave_usage_report_Q3.csv (CSV, 58 KB)
Attachment: draft_term_sheet_edgewave_v1.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)
From: Lena Cruz <lena@edgewave.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing realignment & renewal — proposal for EdgeWave

Marcus,

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the context. The usage file looks right. Our purchasing lead Ray Cooper (purchasing@edgewave.com) and finance (finance@edgewave.com) should be in the loop for any changes to billing cadence or contractual commitments.

A few clarifying asks before a call:
- What exact per-token rates are you holding for 6 months and how does that step after month 6?
- How is burst counted versus guaranteed commit (we need to avoid surprise overage patterns)?
- Can you outline the credit amortization — is the onboarding credit refundable or applied against invoice?

If you can send a short mutual action plan + procurement checklist, I can start the review internally and loop Ray. Call after we share the plan would be helpful — how about Thursday 10/05 at 10am PT?

Best,
Lena Cruz
Head of Product Ops, EdgeWave Systems

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Cruz <lena@edgewave.com>
Date: 2028-10-03T08:26:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pricing realignment & renewal — proposal for EdgeWave

Monica / Ben — forwarding Lena's note and the usage file. Need quick tradeoffs from CS/SE on the proposed guardrails below so I can put firm numbers into the MAP for procurement.

My suggested commercial outline (draft):
- Term: 12 months (start on signature)
- Commit: 1.2M tokens/month (guaranteed)
- Burst band: up to 2.0M tokens/month, billed at base rate + 15% for burst only after guaranteed commit exhausted
- Price hold: per-token rate locked for first 6 months; months 7–12 step up by 5% unless usage stays within predictable bands (we can discuss a softer step mechanism)
- Discount: 10% off list for the duration if they sign the 12-month commit
- Onboarding credit: $50,000 applied as invoice credit across first three billing cycles (non-refundable)

Attachments sent to EdgeWave: draft_term_sheet_edgewave_v1.pdf, EdgeWave_usage_report_Q3.csv

Can you confirm:
1) Technical viability of the burst billing approach and whether we need an SLA carveout for cache-warming spikes
2) Whether the onboarding credit can be applied as a straight invoice credit or if Finance requires a different construct

I want to have a MAP + doc to share with Ray by Thursday morning if possible. Thanks —
Marcus
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing realignment & renewal — proposal for EdgeWave

On Thu, Oct 3, 2028 at 08:26, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com> wrote:
> My suggested commercial outline (draft):
> - Term: 12 months (start on signature)
> - Commit: 1.2M tokens/month (guaranteed)
> - Burst band: up to 2.0M tokens/month, billed at base rate + 15% for burst only after guaranteed commit exhausted
> - Price hold: per-token rate locked for first 6 months; months 7–12 step up by 5% unless usage stays within predictable bands (we can discuss a softer step mechanism)
> - Discount: 10% off list for the duration if they sign the 12-month commit
> - Onboarding credit: $50,000 applied as invoice credit across first three billing cycles (non-refundable)

Marcus — quick check from ops/CS:
- Burst model above is fine technically, but we should add a 24-hour smoothing window to avoid counting transient spikes as burst (i.e., require sustained usage > 125% of baseline for 24 hours before bursting kicks in). That prevents accidental invoice surprises on cache warms.
- Suggest we make the onboarding credit apply as an account-level invoice credit (non-refundable) rather than a one-time rebate to keep bookkeeping simple. Finance should be OK with that; Ben can confirm.
- Also recommend a usage dashboard access and three sample alert thresholds in the term sheet so EdgeWave has visibility before a burst invoice triggers.

Ben — can you confirm the dashboard and the 24-hour smoothing window are implementable in the short term?

Monica Patel
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Lena Cruz <lena@edgewave.com>, Ray Cooper <purchasing@edgewave.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, EdgeWave Finance <finance@edgewave.com>
Date: 2028-10-09T14:32:00-07:00
Subject: Final commercial offer & next steps — EdgeWave renewal (DW-2386)

Lena / Ray — thanks for the conversation last week. Per internal validation we've formalized an offer for your procurement and finance review. Summary (final):

- Term: 12 months (01-Nov-2028 to 31-Oct-2029)
- Base commit: 1.2M tokens/month
- Burst: up to 2.0M tokens/month; burst charging only after 24-hour sustained threshold (smoothing window) and billed at base rate + 15% for burst tokens
- Unit pricing: base list rate $0.0018/token; 10% discount applied across base and burst list (effective base rate $0.00162/token) for entire 12 months
- Price hold: effective per-token rate locked for months 1–6; months 7–12 may step up to 5% unless usage variance remains below agreed band (details in term sheet)
- Onboarding credit: $50,000 applied as invoice credit across first three invoices (non-refundable)
- Visibility: EdgeWave will receive dashboard access and three pre-configured alerts (80%, 100% of commit, sustained spike alert)

Attached: renewal_term_sheet_edgewave_signed_stub.pdf (please note this is the commercial stub — final DocuSign packet is linked below).

Next steps:
1) Ray / procurement to confirm billing contact and PO timing.
2) We will send DocuSign (link below) with the commercial terms; once signed we’ll schedule onboarding and enable the dashboard.
3) Finance to confirm invoice credit application (monica / ben will follow up if any bookkeeping changes needed).

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/example-doc-edgewave
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/2386

If that looks good I'll issue the DocuSign by end of day and loop our renewals ops.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
